title: Evidence Journey Simulator and Custody Validation Workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver an automated 'Evidence Journey Simulator' (EJS) + Custody Validation workflow to validate SOC 2 / ISO 27001 evidence collectors, retention enforcement, and cross-region custody guarantees before production rollouts. The simulator will: 1) synthesize realistic control evidence (access logs, configuration snapshots, signed attestation blobs) according to a control mapping matrix; 2) exercise asynchronous collectors and retention enforcement agents in sandbox regions; 3) validate custody chain via signed manifests (KMS-signed) and provide deterministic + fuzzy checks for artifact integrity; 4) produce a compliance-grade report bundle with proof-of-presence receipts for auditors.

Why this is different: existing work focuses on harvesting and static bundling. EJS proactively simulates failure modes (KMS rotation, cross-region transfer, delayed collector delivery, redaction mistakes) and scores overall compliance readiness. It surfaces latent gaps in collector sequencing, retention TTLs, and evidence redaction policies.

Design summary / key components:
- Control mapping matrix: CSV/Confluence table mapping control IDs (SOC2 CC6.1, ISO27001 A.8.3) to required artifact types and minimal fields. Located at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Compliance/Evidence+Mapping+Matrix
- Synthesizer: service that emits event-streams of synthetic artifacts following configurable profiles (prod-like, PII-heavy, long-retention). Uses protobuf payloads for collector interoperability.
- Async Collector Protocol (ACP): lightweight HTTP+signed-receipt handshake used by sandbox collectors. Spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=763211
- Custody Validator: verifies manifest signatures (KMS ECDSA) and reconstructs custody chain; flags rewrap vs re-encrypt anomalies. Implementation prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12487
- Evidence Packager: bundles artifacts into an auditor-friendly zip with index.json, retention metadata, and tamper-evidence Merkle root.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- EJS can run a full simulation for a 3-region scenario and produce a pass/fail score and a downloadable bundle.
- Custody Validator detects KMS rotation events and produces remediation guidance (re-sign, rewrap) without losing retention metadata.
- Redaction orchestration respects retention windows and creates an audit trail (who redacted, rule id, regex/jmespath used).
- Generated bundles are compatible with existing audit ingestion tooling (see ENG-76133 integration tests).

Trade-offs & decisions:
- Payload format: choose protobuf for stability and schema validation; downside: additional encoding in lightweight collectors. Decision: protobuf v3 with stable JSON mapping for human debugging.
- Where to store simulated artifacts: use dedicated sandbox S3 buckets with region tags rather than production buckets to avoid accidental leakage. Retention enforcement is applied via lifecycle rules and TTL metadata.
- Signature model: KMS-based ECDSA provides non-repudiation but key rotation requires rewrap flow. We will prototype a 'signature rewrap' service to preserve proof continuity.

Operational runbook snippets (examples):
- Simulate delayed collector: curl -X POST https://ejs.sandbox.redwood.ai/simulate -d '{"profile":"delayed-collectors","duration_seconds":3600}'
- Validate a bundle locally: python tools/validate_bundle.py --input bundle-2025-11-18.zip --kms-key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/abc

Related artifacts:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Compliance/EJS+PRD
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12487
- Design diagrams: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_DesignDiagrams
- Sandbox dashboard (sim runs): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/comp-ejs/sim-runs

Open questions:
- Should the simulator intentionally inject partial redactions (to test auditor tolerance)? Proposal: include as a toggle in advanced runs.
- SLA for rewrap service: synchronous vs async? Proposal: async with compensating transactions recorded in the evidence index.

Next steps:
- Finalize protobuf schema and publish ACP spec (owner: ENG infra)
- Build minimal EJS UI in Console for selecting simulation profiles (owner: UX + PM)
- Wire Custody Validator into evidence packager and run end-to-end smoke tests against ENG-76133 test harness
